title: The docker e2e harness hard-codes the built-in type set, so every new type reddens a required context
description:
Follow-up found while adding the Standard type (LCLI-687, DEC-167 (3)). docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh hard-codes the built-in type vocabulary, so every new built-in type reddens the REQUIRED `docker e2e harness (real lore + backlog binaries)` context until the harness is edited by hand.

Concretely, in docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh: the Phase-17 LCLI-299 AC3 probe asserts an exact schema count (`.data.count == 10`, which LCLI-687 had to bump to 11) and lists every expected `*.schema.json` path literally; and four loops enumerate the slugs (`for T in epic arc story spec adr runbook reference constitution constants attested-computation; do`). LCLI-687's Standard type broke the required context on exactly the count assertion, and the fix was a hand edit of the count, the file list and the four loops.

Acceptance: the harness derives the expected set from the CLI itself — `lore types` and/or `lore schema export` — rather than a literal slug list or a hard-coded count, so the coverage and count assertions move with the active profile. Low priority: this is hardening, so it waits.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh derives its expected schema set — the count and the paths, and the slugs its loops iterate — from the CLI itself (`lore types` and/or `lore schema export`) rather than a literal slug list or a hard-coded count.

A positive control shows a new built-in type needs NO harness edit: with the set sourced from the CLI, the Phase-17 LCLI-299 count/coverage assertions follow a changed profile without editing run-e2e.sh.

plan: 1. Derive the expected committed-schema set (slugs + count) ONCE in Phase 17 from the CLI exporter itself, not lore types -- a deprecated alias (Story -> Arc, LCLI-553) owns a schema file lore types does not name.
2. Replace the four literal slug loops and the AC3 hard-coded count/path list with the derived values; leave the AC2 alias-pair probe (invariant to the profile) with a comment saying why.
3. Pin it in test/docker-e2e-guard.test.ts: no literal slug list / count for the schema set, plus a positive control showing the derived set follows a profile with an added type (AC#2).
4. Gates: bash -n, shellcheck, the derivation measurement, bun test, lore check. Review, record, land.
implementationNotes: Completed on branch fix/LCLI-688-derive-schema-set. WHAT CHANGED: docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh now DERIVES its expected committed-schema set from the CLI instead of a literal. Phase 17 captures `lore schema export --json` into SCHEMA_JSON, derives SCHEMA_SLUGS from `.data.files[].path` (strip directory plus `.schema.json`), and computes SCHEMA_COUNT; a check asserts the derivation is NON-EMPTY, so a derivation that read nothing cannot let every loop below pass vacuously. The four literal loops now iterate "${SCHEMA_SLUGS[@]}", and the LCLI-299 AC3 assertion compares `.data.count` against $SCHEMA_COUNT and the paths against $LCLI299_EXPECTED_PATHS, derived from the same export with the --out prefix swapped. WHY THE EXPORTER AND NOT `lore types`: a deprecated alias owns a schema file `lore types` does not name (Story -> Arc, LCLI-553), so the set is 11 files for 10 types -- measured locally, `lore schema export` reports 11 files while `lore types` reports 10 slugs. DELIBERATELY LEFT LITERAL, with a comment saying so: the LCLI-299 AC2 probe (count == 2, arc + story). Those two are the ALIAS PAIR for ONE type, invariant to the profile, so a new built-in type does not move them. EVIDENCE: the AC3 assertion construction was simulated locally -- expected paths built from one export EQUAL the actual paths of another with the prefix swapped (EQUAL=YES, count 11); a positive control in test/docker-e2e-guard.test.ts runs a real `lore schema export` over a minimal bundle whose profile declares one MORE type and shows the added type appear in the data the harness reads (reference alone, then reference + qa-plan), so no harness edit is needed; the structural pin reds if a literal slug list or a hard-coded count returns (mutation-verified, 1 fail). GATES: full suite 4988 tests / 2 skip / 0 fail; bash -n; shellcheck via bun run lint:shell clean; lint, typecheck, lore check green. NOT RUN: the docker e2e harness itself -- it is container-only and refuses a host checkout -- so the change was verified by syntax, shellcheck, the derivation simulation and the pin, not by a container run.
finalSummary: docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh no longer hard-codes the built-in type set: Phase 17 derives the expected committed-schema set from `lore schema export --json` itself -- the slugs from .data.files[].path, the count from that set, and the LCLI-299 AC3 assertion compares against both -- so a new built-in type moves the REQUIRED `docker e2e harness` context with no harness edit. The exporter, not `lore types`, is the authority: a deprecated alias owns a schema file `lore types` does not name (Story -> Arc, LCLI-553; 11 files for 10 types). The AC2 alias-pair probe stays literal BY DESIGN, with a comment saying why. Verified by a local simulation of the AC3 assertion (expected paths built from one export equal another with the prefix swapped), by a positive control in test/docker-e2e-guard.test.ts that exports a bundle whose profile declares an ADDED type and shows it appear in the derived data, and by a structural pin that reds if a literal list or count returns (mutation-verified). Full suite 4988 tests / 2 skip / 0 fail; bash -n, shellcheck via lint:shell, lint, typecheck and lore check green. The container harness itself was NOT run -- it is container-only and refuses a host checkout. Run job-0y0elim.
